target_customer: Small e-commerce merchants that need warehousing and fulfillment
problem: Small merchants cannot easily get instant, all-in pricing for warehousing, transportation and shipping. Shotput exposed fulfillment pricing and ordering through a Warehouse API.
business_model: Fulfillment services sold through an API with per-order pricing

founders.name: Praful Mathur
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch says both founders are Northeastern graduates.

founders.name: James Steinberg
founders.background_notes: Quoted in the YC launch post calling Shotput Amazon Web Services for fulfillment.

exit.reason: No shutdown announcement found. CB Insights says it ceased operations and YC lists Inactive.

competitors.name: Shipwire
competitors.what: Palo Alto fulfillment and warehousing provider, acquired by Ingram Micro in 2013

competitors.name: Flexe
competitors.what: Seattle warehouse space marketplace renting by the pallet, founded 2013

technical_complexity.rationale: An API and pricing layer over partner warehouses is standard engineering, but operating real fulfillment with physical partners adds operational difficulty for two people.

defensibility.rationale: As a software layer over rented warehouse capacity it could be copied by existing fulfillment providers, and no data or network moat is documented.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: TechCrunch named Shipwire, UPS and FedEx as established competition. No source shows any of them copying or buying Shotput.

market_need_then: Small online merchants wanted warehousing without a long contract. The YC post frames it as AWS for fulfillment, but no spend or complaint data was cited.

branding.domain_note: Used theshotput.com, which now returns 404. Shotput is also an athletics event, and unrelated firms use similar names.

identity.voice_and_tone: AWS for fulfillment positioning in YC and TechCrunch coverage

branding.brand_signature: The phrase AWS for logistics used in press

brand_strength.rationale: Launch coverage from TechCrunch, VentureBeat and the YC blog, but no brand assets or community evidence were found. The name is a shared word for a sport.

outcome_analysis: Shotput came out of YC Summer 2015 with an AWS for fulfillment pitch, raised only the reported YC seed of about 120K, and is now inactive. The YC page and a startup directory describe later AI and robotics for logistics positioning, but no source dates a pivot. No shutdown cause is public, so failure factors are left empty.
notes: Website theshotput.com returned 404 (dead). The 120K seed rests on a single database (CB Insights, Y Combinator the only investor) and a startup directory repeats the figure; one source claims a 2018 shutdown with about 2M burned, which is unverified and not recorded. Flexe source is dated about two months after the batch. The YC page's later AI and robotics tagline conflicts with the 2015 warehouse API description.
